title: Technical Value Briefing and C‑Suite Elevator Messaging for Enterprise Buyers
author: Leah Martinez
summary: A single-page briefing and supporting collateral to enable sales and solutions engineering to deliver a concise technical value pitch to executive stakeholders (CRO/CTO/CPO) and the accompanying demo + ROI narrative for Redwood Inference's enterprise offers.
body:
Purpose:
This doc provides an executive-level elevator, a short technical brief for decision makers, a demo checklist designed to surface Redwood Inference's economic and reliability advantages, a concise competitive positioning matrix, pricing guidance templates, and a short security FAQ tailored for prospect conversations.

Structure (use this in a 10–15 minute executive briefing):
1) 60‑second elevator for C‑suite
   - For CROs: 'Reduce AI feature unit cost and unpredictability while preserving response quality — Redwood unifies inference across hosted, reserved, and private environments so your product teams can ship faster with predictable economics and SLA-backed reliability.'
   - For CTOs: 'A production-first inference runtime with smart routing, prefix/KV caching, and cost-aware controls that reduce per-token spend by up to 3x on typical dialog workloads while maintaining <150ms median token latency.'
   - For CPOs: 'Ship consistent model behavior across environments with built-in rollouts and quality guards, enabling safe experimentation without regressions or engineering overhead.'

2) Technical brief (2–3 slides' worth of content)
   - Key capabilities to highlight: serving runtime optimizations (continuous batching, KV cache + prefix caching), compilation/kernel selection, automated routing (latency/cost/region policies), and deployment parity (hosted/dedicated/private).
   - Measurable outcomes: predictable latency SLOs (p50/p95 targets), cost reduction levers (batching + cache + quantization profiles), and operational visibility (per‑token cost, request tracing, model-level rollouts).
   - Suggested SLOs to quote: 99.5% request success rate; p95 token latency < 250ms for standard conversational payloads; 99.9% availability for Dedicated plans (call out SLA tiers in pricing).

3) Demo checklist (SE playbook — 12–18 minute live demo)
   - Prep: provision a demo tenant on Redwood Hosted or Dedicated staging. Load a short product-style prompt set (10–12 prompts) and a small evaluation harness.
   - Flow:
      1. 90s: Exec elevator (use CRO/CTO/PPO variant).
      2. 3min: Live inference — show p50/p95 latency and token breakdown in Console while generating responses for the prompt set.
      3. 3min: Cost story — enable batch and cache, re-run sample and show delta in per‑token estimate.
      4. 3min: Reliability & rollouts — trigger a canary rollout to a new model version, demonstrate automatic fallback policy.
      5. 2min: Security & deployment options — show VPC flow, KMS key binding example.
      6. 2min: Q&A focused on procurement and next steps.
   - Artifacts to share post-demo: short ROI one-pager, sample contract language for Dedicated/Private, and a configuration YAML snippet for a customer's typical traffic profile.

4) Competitive positioning (short brief)
   - Primary claim: 'Production-first economics and unified deployment parity' — vs managed endpoint vendors (who focus on model access but not cost controls) and vs self-hosted runtimes (who require heavy ops investment).
   - Differentiators to call out live:
      - Transparent per-token unit economics and tooling to reduce unit costs (batching, KV prefix caching, quantization guidance).
      - Rollout and quality-guard rails integrated into the control plane (A/B, canary, regression alerts on test prompts).
      - Flexible deployments with consistent API & tooling across Hosted, Dedicated, Private.
   - Quick objection responses: competitor claims of lower latency — respond with: 'Latency wins depend on placement and workload; we provide predictable p95 targets and automated routing to meet business SLAs, and we publish model performance profiles for baseline comparisons.'

5) Pricing guidance (how to discuss economics in discovery)
   - Pricing levers to surface: model selection (open vs fine-tuned), deployment mode (hosted vs dedicated vs private), commitment level (monthly/annual), and add‑ons (longer observability retention, SLA uplift).
   - Sample commercial tiers (talking numbers for discovery — adjust per-customer):
      - Hosted Starter: pay-as-you-go; $0.0008/token equivalent for chat workloads; ideal for PoC.
      - Dedicated Base: committed monthly GPU capacity; baseline includes 99.9% uptime SLA and dedicated model cache; example: $25k/month for 4x A100 equivalent capacity (for scaled but predictable inference).
      - Private Enterprise: license + support; includes on-prem image, KMS/HSM integration, and extended retention: custom quoting.
   - Quick ROI model (illustrative):
      - Assumptions: 10M tokens/month, current cost $0.0012/token, current p95 latency 400ms, projected with Redwood: $0.0006/token (50% savings), p95 180ms.
      - Monthly savings: (0.0012-0.0006)*10,000,000 = $6,000/month => $72k/year (token-cost savings alone).
      - Additional upside: reduced engineering time for ops (~0.5 FTE/year estimated) and fewer incidents. Use these numbers openly as directional — replace with customer telemetry during scoping.

6) Case study capsule (1 page)
   - Headline: "FinTech SaaS reduced inference costs by 3x and decreased model rollback incidents by 80%"
   - Customer background: mid-market SaaS company providing conversational financial guidance, operating in US/EU.
   - Problem: unpredictable costs under varying traffic patterns and slow model rollouts that caused regressions.
   - Solution: migrated to Redwood Dedicated with KV prefix caching and canary rollouts; adopted recommended quantization profile for the target model.
   - Outcomes: 3x lower per-token spend in sustained traffic windows, p95 latency down from 420ms to 170ms, and a 3-month time-to-rollout improvement for model experiments.
   - Quote to use: 'Redwood let us ship features without cost surprises and gave the product team confidence to iterate' — Head of Engineering (redacted).

7) Security FAQ (short answers for prospect calls)
   - Q: Can Redwood operate inside our VPC/on-prem?
     A: Yes — Redwood Private supports VPC-deployed control planes and an on-prem package. We provide deployment automation and hardened images for air-gapped installs.
   - Q: How are keys managed?
     A: We support customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations for Private and Dedicated deployments; Hosted supports envelope encryption with optional customer KMS for key rotation.
   - Q: Where does data persist and how long?
     A: Default retention windows are configurable; hosted defaults keep request logs for 30 days, dedicated options can be extended or disabled. We provide data residency controls per region and enterprise contracts for extended retention or deletion guarantees.
   - Q: Can we prevent model leakage or prompt data retention?
     A: Yes — prefix/KV caching can be scoped per-tenant and patched to avoid sensitive data in shared caches; we also provide scrubbers and redaction hooks in the ingestion pipeline.
   - Q: What compliance evidence do you provide?
     A: SOC2 Type II report, penetration test summaries, and customer-facing compliance pack on request (see security-and-compliance/audit-logging for details).

8) Objection handling (brief scripts)
   - 'We will self-host to save money' → 'Self-hosting front-loads engineering and ops cost; we can show a 6–12 month TCO comparison that includes developer time and production incidents.'
   - 'Your pricing seems complex' → 'We map pricing to the levers customers care about (throughput, latency, control) and can run a pilot to produce an exact estimate using your traffic profile.'

9) Next steps checklist for AE/SE after a qualifying discovery call
   - 1) Run sample telemetry-based ROI with SE using customer's 7‑day traffic snapshot.
   - 2) Provision demo tenant and populate with 8–12 representative prompts.
   - 3) Share one-page ROI + SOW template and schedule executive 20‑minute briefing.
   - 4) If security-sensitive, initiate security questionnaire with Security team and share SOC2 + pen test artifacts.

Document maintenance: update the pricing numbers and sample ROI quarterly or when commercial rates change. SEs should append any customer-specific numbers to the saved ROI template in the shared drive.
positioning_statements: Production-first inference runtime that optimizes cost and reliability for product teams.
Unified API and tooling across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private to avoid rework during scale.
Operational levers (batching, cache, quantization) that translate into measurable unit-economics improvements.
competitive_highlights: Against managed model endpoints: emphasize cost controls and rollouts. Against self-hosted runtimes: emphasize lower ops burden, observability, and predictable SLAs. Against single-cloud AI endpoints: emphasize deployment parity and routing for multi-region resiliency.
demo_deck_outline: Slide 1: Executive elevator + outcomes. Slide 2: Current customer pain (cost, latency, regressions). Slide 3: How Redwood solves it — runtime + control plane. Slide 4: Live demo artifacts (Console views). Slide 5: Pricing & ROI sample. Slide 6: Security & next steps.
pricing_guidance: Use the commercial tiers as discovery anchors. Always convert to customer tokens/week and model type. Offer a 30–60 day pilot with transparent usage dashboards before committing to a Dedicated plan.
case_studies: See full FinTech case study in confluence://sales-enablement/case-studies/fintech-cost-and-reliability-2025. Use the capsule above as an executive summary during outreach.
security_faq: SOC2 Type II, KMS/HSM support, VPC/private control plane, configurable retention, scrubbers and redaction hooks. For sensitive prospects, route to Security team and request the compliance pack before legal review.
